purpose: Steps 1-3 implementation summary: the new live orchestration module, and the real application trigger wiring it into an actual user-facing action.

filesAdded.role: runContractAnalysis - the composition entry point. Contains ONLY sequencing/composition logic: fetches Document rows, re-parses each one's stored bytes, calls the real compiler modules in the verified dependency order (14-live-contract-analysis-architecture.json), and records AnalysisRun/ClaimReviewItem state. Zero re-implemented analytical logic - every judgment call (what is a covenant, what is ambiguous, what needs review) is delegated to the existing modules.
Domain types + CONTRACT_DOCUMENT_TYPE_SET (the disclosed Document.type scope - see 19-contract-truth-ownership-map.json).

filesModified.change: runExtractionAction now also calls runContractAnalysis({companyId, triggeringDocumentId: documentId}) immediately after the pre-existing runExtractionForDocument call, wrapped in a defense-in-depth try/catch so an unexpected exception here can never break the pre-existing extraction wizard's own redirect/UX.
filesModified.whyThisActionAndNotUploadDocumentAction: runContractAnalysis re-parses each document's own bytes directly from storage (never from lib/extraction/**'s chunk output - see the ingestion-step note below), so it has NO real dependency on the legacy extraction pipeline's own output and could technically be triggered at upload time instead. It was placed on the Extraction-stage action instead of the Documents-stage upload action for two reasons: (1) uploadDocumentAction's whole job today is a fast, synchronous store-and-chunk operation with no existing precedent for kicking off a multi-stage AI pipeline inline - runExtractionForDocument is this codebase's own existing precedent for 'the button a user clicks to kick off real analysis of an uploaded document', so composing onto that action keeps the UX mental model ('Documents -> upload; Extraction -> analyze') intact rather than silently starting a second, invisible pipeline the instant a file is dropped; (2) it lets a single already-uploaded document be (re-)analyzed by re-clicking the existing Extraction button, without a separate new UI surface, which this bounded workstream's charter explicitly rules out ('no UI work').

genuineIntegrationBugFoundAndFixed.discoveredWhile: Composing scripts/phase-3f-first-blind-run.ts's own proven call sequence into this orchestrator - that frozen certification script was read as the concrete reference for 'what does a real, working call to buildCovenantContextBundle/compileCovenantToIR actually look like'.
genuineIntegrationBugFoundAndFixed.bug: The reference script builds operativeSourceText as `candidate.structuralNodeKeys.map((k) => index.getNodeText(k, "DESCENDANTS")).join("\n\n")`. `structuralNodeKeys` is DiscoveredCandidate's own explicitly @deprecated, label-shaped field (`${documentId}::${sectionRef}` - never guaranteed unique). `StructuralIndex.getNodeText(nodeId, mode)` looks its argument up via a real physical-occurrence-id map (`nodesById.get(nodeId)` in structural-index.ts) - a label-shaped key never matches that map, so `getNodeText` silently returns "" (its own documented behavior for an unrecognized id) for EVERY candidate the reference script compiles. This means the frozen script's own semantic compiler calls were built with an EMPTY operativeSourceText string for every candidate - a real, silent defect in that script (not merely a hypothetical one), independently confirmed by reading structural-index.ts's own getNodeText implementation line by line.
genuineIntegrationBugFoundAndFixed.fix: This orchestrator uses `candidate.structuralNodeIds` (DiscoveredCandidate's own occurrence-safe, real-node-id counterpart field, per that field's own doc comment) instead of `structuralNodeKeys` when calling `index.getNodeText`.
genuineIntegrationBugFoundAndFixed.scopeOfFix: Minimal and localized to this new orchestrator file only - scripts/phase-3f-first-blind-run.ts itself (a frozen certification artifact under a different, already-completed phase) was NOT touched, per this phase's own 'production code the certification depends on stays frozen' discipline; this finding is disclosed here rather than silently worked around, and is the only genuine integration-blocking bug found while wiring Workstreams A-E's modules together - no other module required any change to compose correctly.
genuineIntegrationBugFoundAndFixed.verifiedBy: tests/contract-model/live-contract-analysis-orchestrator.test.ts's NEGATIVE CASE test - with this fix, a real, scripted candidate compiles with its own real source text and reaches genuine end-to-end verification (VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND); confirmed by direct debugging (a throwaway tsx script) that the bug reproduces exactly as described when structuralNodeKeys is used instead.

callerInjectionDesign.shape: runContractAnalysis(input, {callers?}) accepts optional {discoveryCaller, amendmentCaller, verificationCaller, semanticCaller, aiInventoryCaller} - each defaults to the real, env-var-driven getStageCaller()/getSemanticCaller() when omitted (which themselves safely fall back to a zero-cost, zero-fabrication synthetic implementation off Vercel with no credential configured, and throw loudly ON Vercel with no credential - unchanged, pre-existing behavior this orchestrator relies on rather than reimplements).
callerInjectionDesign.rationale: The real application action (app/[companyId]/onboarding/documents/actions.ts) never passes this option - production always uses the real env-var-driven callers, exactly as every other real caller of these modules already does. The option exists solely so this new module's own tests can inject deterministic ScriptedStageCaller/ScriptedSemanticCaller test doubles (the exact, pre-existing test convention this codebase already established in tests/contract-model/phase-2f2-discovery-schema-robustness.test.ts), never a mock of PRODUCTION logic itself.

documentIngestionDesign.decision: Each document's full text is obtained by re-fetching its stored bytes (getDocumentStorageProvider().retrieve(document.storageRef)) and re-running the SAME parseDocument(bytes, contentType) function lib/onboarding/documents.ts's own uploadAndChunkDocument already used at upload time - never by reconstructing text from persisted DocumentChunk rows.
documentIngestionDesign.whyNotChunks: lib/extraction/chunk.ts's own chunker deliberately OVERLAPS adjacent chunks (OVERLAP_CHARS = 500, its own documented reason: 'so a cross-reference near a sub-split boundary stays interpretable from either side'). Naively concatenating chunk.text in original order would duplicate up to 500 characters at every chunk boundary for any document longer than MAX_CHUNK_CHARS (6000) - which is every real credit agreement - corrupting the exact charStart/charEnd offsets structural-index.ts's own physical-occurrence identity discipline depends on being correct. Re-parsing the immutable original bytes is the single, already-proven-correct source of truth both this orchestrator and the original upload pipeline agree on.
